Independent contributor pre-check for head `3c0dc8eb7406aaaea4ccb752c8989c3e7c94284d`.

No actionable findings remain.

The two G43.4 posts apply the resolved rotary sign once, when they write the angle. The pose travel check uses the same convention. ToolRh output stays unchanged. Existing Mach4 coverage passes.

Local Windows validation with Rust 1.100.1:

- All 97 mapped quick test steps pass: 1,978 passed tests and six expected ignored tests. Only two redundant prebuilds were omitted.
- All six issue pins pass in the `script_rotary` suite: 72 passed, zero failed or ignored.
- All 11 light twins pass in five actual test steps. Only the redundant prebuild was omitted.
- The P1 heavy target passes its actual ignored test, `every_slow_kind_on_a_mill_turn_keeps_the_work_spindle_within_the_chuck`: one passed, zero failed.
- Post all-targets clippy passes with warnings denied. The diff check and both touched test-file format checks pass.

The formatter differences in `judge.rs` are identical to the baseline. No new formatting difference is introduced.

Explicit C live-tool input keeps its counted capability warning. App posting blocks that warning. The standalone post CLI keeps its existing warning-output behavior. Existing app tests confirm warning blocking and no written files on a per-operation refusal.

The post subtree guidance and stream contract were checked. Graphify was unavailable; no generated graph update ran. No full heavy lane, release-cut gate or physical machine trial ran.

This is an independent contributor pre-check. It is not a counted collaborator review or approval.

Reviewer: MacBook-Pro.local pool job review-4473, claude-opus-5-5, mkinney (pool seat bob); did not write or refresh this PR.

**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a SAFETY-tier review: the PR changes posted G-code (two posts) and the machine pose check.

## What looks good

- `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps`: `angleWord` applies the resolved convention at the one place that writes a rotary word. All rotary words go through it: the initial pose, the modal words, the indexed A path (Doosan) and the held-letter unwind (`angleWord(held[i], 0)`). The modal memory (`lastA`/`lastB`/`lastC`) keeps the stream value, so the modal test does not change. A `-0` formats as `0.` (`toFixed`), so the unwind word does not get a sign.
- The convention resolves in one place (`machine_rotary.rs` `props_rotaries_and_rtcp`): the axis value, then the machine value, then `tool_rh`. The posts read only the resolved per-rotary word. The judge uses `Machine::effective_sign_convention` with the same order.
- `judge.rs`: the letter path and the lone-X path negate after the direction sign. The diagnostic sentence names the signed angle that the post writes.
- `tool_rh` output stays byte-identical. `g43_4_tool_rh_keeps_the_default_program` pins this, and `script_goldens`, `example_catalog` and all app posting suites are green. No recorded program (`*.nc`, `*.cl`, `examples/catalog/**`) changed. No goldens moved.
- The body is complete: readings, six named pins, what was not exercised, `Changelog:`, `Fixes #4436`, a decision record. The commit subjects are conventional. There is no process file, no dependency, no snapshot PNG and no `CHANGELOG.md` edit. The new test file has a provenance line and a gate map. It is 333 lines.

## Results, merged with main (locally, macOS)

Trial merge: PR head `3c0dc8eb7` + upstream/main `2394b5ad1`. The merge was clean.

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (100 steps: post build, 9 post suites, app build, 88 app suites, site tests) | 100 ok, 0 failed |
| `post suites: script_rotary` (has the six pins) | ok |
| `app suites: example_catalog` | ok |
| `post suites: script_goldens` | ok |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Extra suites run: none were owed. The diff does not touch `testdata/` or importer code.

Heavy lanes: not run. They are not a merge condition. The author reports `app heavy: lathe_workholding_kinds` green on Windows.

## Mutations (run by this reviewer)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `fanuc.cps` `angleWord` writes `v` without the convention | RED: `g43_4_posts_use_machine_and_axis_sign_conventions`, `g43_4_travel_check_judges_the_posted_sign` |
| `judge.rs` `pose_problems` letter path without the negation | RED: `g43_4_travel_check_judges_the_posted_sign` |
| `judge.rs` `x_rotary_problem` lone-X path without the negation | RED: `lone_x_travel_applies_convention_after_the_axis_direction`, `tormach_refuses_its_own_word_outside_the_signed_travel` |

All mutations were reverted. The tree was clean before the review was posted.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Follow-ups (file after merge)

1. **`tormach.cps` ignores `table_rh` (suggest P1, pre-existing, `effort:high`).** The judge change applies to every post. `tormach.cps` (`aRotary`, `toolAngle`) does not read `signConvention`. The PR's own pin `tormach_refuses_its_own_word_outside_the_signed_travel` shows the result: on a `table_rh` lone-X machine the check now judges `A-20`, and the post writes `A20`. Tormach's own travel check refuses its word when it is outside the travel, so the PR does not let an unsafe word pass. On a travel that holds both signs, Tormach writes the angle with the tool-relative sign on a `table_rh` table. That is the same defect as #4436, and it existed before this PR. The PR does not make it worse: in some cases the check now refuses where it passed before. This is not a blocker for this PR.
2. **Mach4 and the judge on a `table_rh` A/C trunnion (suggest P7, research).** `mach4.cps` solves its own pose and checks its own words against the travel (`inBounds`). The judge now judges the negated letter for `table_rh`. A mismatch can only refuse a pose; it cannot pass an unsafe word. A test that runs `MachineCheck` and the Mach4 post on one `table_rh` trunnion would show if the two agree.

## Notes

- No shipped machine in `assets/machines/` states `table_rh`, so only user machine files reach the new behaviour.
- The PR is ready and not a draft. The author is not a collaborator, so the maintainer approves and merges by hand.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Heads-up from qsmits, for the merge order (no change asked on this PR).

PR #4499 (#4417, P1, ready for review) also changes the G43.4 output of `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps`. It solves the joint angles of an A-outer tilt chain (A carries B) in a new prelude function `chainAngles` (`crates/post/src/post/tilt_chain.rs`), and `judge.rs::pose_problems` judges the same angles through `crates/post/src/machine/tilt_chain.rs::joint_angles`.

This PR applies the rotary sign convention in the same posts. Whichever PR merges second must merge `main` and check that the two rules combine: first the joint angles for the real chain, then the sign of each rotary. The machine check must judge the result of both. One point from the pre-review of #4499 may also matter here: an A+B pose on a table-table or table-and-head chain is only covered by argument, not by a test.
